partial_progress.details: Completed Phase 9 (Shared Corpus Enumeration) and Phase 10 (Flip run-all.sh's Default to Parallel). Phase 9: added gate_registry_shared_corpus_build (gate-registry-lib.sh, producer -- one `git ls-files` per invocation) and common_shared_corpus_available/common_shared_corpus_files (common.sh, consumer -- per-lint glob filter over the shared corpus); wired into verify-deploy.sh (built once, exported, EXIT-trap-cleaned, gated on the real lib having loaded before any degrade-safe stub assignment). All 6 affected lints (lint-shellcheck.sh, lint-state-writer-boundary.sh, lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh, lint-directory-pathspec-boundary.sh, lint-hook-registration-paths.sh, lint-task-lookup-adoption.sh) gained a shared-corpus fast path that engages ONLY on an unmodified default scan with no explicit scan-path argument, falling through to each lint's pre-existing enumeration otherwise -- standalone invocability and the find-based fixture fallback are both fully preserved and re-verified (0 regressions across all 6 lints' own fixture suites). Caught and fixed a real bug during verification: a naive multi-segment glob for lint-task-lookup-adoption.sh's commands/skills/agents scope also matched an unrelated, deeply-nested 'agents' directory (lean/context/project/lean4/agents/*.md) -- found as a 423-vs-425-file discrepancy against the real corpus, fixed with an exact structural per-candidate check. Added cases 22-25 to test-gate-registry-resolution.sh (26/26 passing) proving the plumbing and a seeded SC2155 violation is detected via both the shared-corpus fast path and the pre-existing fallback. Disclosed, verified-harmless scope narrowing: switching 5 lints to a git-tracked-only corpus excludes 15 vendored, gitignored LICENSE.md files under a Python venv that `find` previously scanned; confirmed zero matches for any affected lint's detection pattern. Phase 10: flipped run-all.sh's JOBS default from 1 to 'auto' (a pure default-value change -- 'auto' already had a correct resolution branch); preserved --jobs 1 as the unchanged, byte-identical sequential opt-out; recorded the work-bound/straggler-bound JOBS_CAP=4 rationale in the header; added cases 8-10 to test-run-all-parallel.sh (12/12 passing) pinning the new default's genuine concurrency, the RUN_ALL_NESTED guard still forcing sequential under the bare invocation specifically, and --jobs 1's continued byte-identical output. Fixed a real, pre-existing gap discovered during this phase's own gate-3 verification pass: 8 files created across this task's earlier phases 4/6/8/9 (gate-registry.data, lib/gate-registry-lib.sh, lib/gate-verdict-extract-lib.sh, lint/lint-gate-registry.sh, measure-gate-costs.sh, tests/test-gate-registry-resolution.sh, tests/test-lint-shellcheck-parallel.sh, tests/test-measure-gate-costs.sh) were never registered in manifest.json's provides.scripts array -- added all 8. Two files touched outside this task's declared file_scope (common.sh, manifest.json) were committed as explicit, disclosed, narrow follow-up commits with issue-record.sh entries (class: scope excursion, severity: minor), per the Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check's drop-and-warn design. Phase 11 (redeploy, idle-machine measured before/after, full-gate verification) remains, deliberately not attempted: two bounded local-background-waiter attempts at a complete `verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 8` run (~19 minutes total, confirmed genuinely progressing via ps --forest, not stalled) were terminated cleanly under heavy ambient contention from concurrently-active sibling sessions in this shared environment (host load climbed from ~1.5 to 12+ during the wait). Phase 11 is explicitly chartered to redo this exact full-battery check properly, once, on an actually-idle host (load<2) -- duplicating it here under contention would have produced an invalid measurement per the dispatch's own stated contention-invalidates-measurements requirement.

completion_data.completion_summary: Completed phases 9 and 10 of the 11-phase gate-framework refactor: shared tracked-file corpus enumeration across 6 lints (one git ls-files per verify-deploy.sh invocation instead of six redundant walks) and run-all.sh's default flipped from sequential to auto-parallel, with full regression coverage and two real pre-existing bugs (a path-matching glob over-match; a manifest.json registration gap spanning this task's own earlier phases) caught and fixed during verification. Phase 11 (redeploy + idle-machine measured verification) remains.

memory_candidates.content: When filtering a flat corpus list (NUL-delimited relative paths from `git ls-files`) by a glob pattern via bash's `[[ str == pattern ]]`/`case`, remember that `*` spans directory separators freely -- it is NOT find's single-path-segment `-name` semantics. A pattern like 'ext/*/agents/*.md' intended to match exactly one path segment between 'ext/' and 'agents/' will ALSO match a deeply-nested, unrelated directory several levels down that happens to be named 'agents' anywhere later in the path. Caught live via a small but real file-count discrepancy (423 vs 425) when comparing the glob-filtered corpus against a known-good find-based baseline on the REAL corpus -- a synthetic fixture with only 1-2 levels of nesting would never have surfaced this. Fix: an exact structural check (strip the known prefix, take exactly the first remaining path segment, and match the literal remainder against the exact expected sub-path), not a looser multi-segment glob. General lesson: when migrating a `find`-based enumeration to a flat-corpus glob filter, always diff file COUNTS (not just violation counts) against the find-based baseline on the real corpus before trusting the glob is correctly scoped to the intended depth.

verify-deploy.sh's gate-3 (deploy-content-drift / manifest-registration check) checks that every file on disk under an extension is registered in that extension's manifest.json `provides.scripts` array. A new script or test suite added mid-task, without a dedicated phase step to update manifest.json, silently accumulates as an unregistered-file gap that only surfaces the next time gate 3 is actually run against the real corpus -- which can be several phases later if the task's own interim verification only ever runs the narrower --only-gate check for the specific gate it's touching. When a plan's implementation phases create new source-store files (a new lib, a new lint, a new test suite), add a step (or a recurring verification habit) to immediately register each new path in the owning extension's manifest.json provides.scripts, rather than deferring it to a later full-battery run where it surfaces as an unrelated-looking gate-3 finding and must be traced back across several prior phases.

On a shared, multi-session host, a bounded local-background-waiter check on a long-running process (ps --forest + kill -0 liveness polling) can reveal genuine, non-stalled progress (different child suites cycling through over successive checks) even while a naive 'has it finished yet' poll looks unproductive. Before concluding a long-running verification is hung or abandoning the wait, inspect the process tree directly rather than just the elapsed time or an empty/quiet log file (a --quiet-mode tool may legitimately produce zero output until completion). Conversely, when `uptime`'s load average climbs sharply during the wait (e.g. 1.5 -> 12+) with no corresponding change in what THIS dispatch is running, that is strong, checkable evidence of cross-session contention from other concurrently-active agents in the same environment, not a regression in the code under test -- worth confirming via `uptime` before attributing a slow or inconclusive run to the change being verified.
